answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent to scale the network. The verifier acts as a geologic monitor; it treats every new identity like an isolated island of logic, rejecting any reused output to prevent sybil clusters. While an honest participant pays this flat cost, an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a hard karst layer of computational exhaustion. Each thread must anchor its unique crystal of proof to the ledger. Failure triggers a permanent identity burn, enforcing non-collusion.
